title: Influence of postoperative acute kidney injury on one-year health-related quality of life of patients after cardiac surgery: prospective, observational study
summary:
More than 100,000 cardiac surgical procedures are performed in Germany each year. The primary aims of these procedures are to prolong patients' lives and improve their quality of life. At the same time, cardiac surgery is a major procedure and is associated with certain risks. One common complication is a temporary or persistent decline in kidney function (acute kidney injury, AKI), which affects approximately one in four patients. Even if kidney function initially recovers, AKI may increase the long-term risk of cardiovascular disease and recurrent kidney problems.
Postoperative AKI may also have a negative impact on patients' health-related quality of life. However, only limited contemporary data are available on this topic.

The purpose of this study is to assess health-related quality of life over a one-year period in patients undergoing cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB). "Quality of life" refers to how patients perceive their own health and well-being in everyday life. This includes physical functioning, emotional well-being, the ability to perform daily activities, social participation, and any symptoms or limitations experienced. These aspects will be assessed using standardized questionnaires.

The study will compare health-related quality of life between patients who develop postoperative acute kidney injury and those who do not.
Participation in the study will last approximately one year for each participant.
Participants will be contacted before surgery and again on postoperative days 28, 90, 180, and 365. During these contacts, they will be asked questions about their health-related quality of life. Completing the questionnaire takes approximately 15 minutes, and the same questionnaire will be used at each assessment.
In addition, participants will be asked about their general health status and any hospital readmissions that may have occurred since the previous follow-up. Each follow-up interview is expected to take approximately 20 minutes. Participants will receive a total of four follow-up telephone calls after surgery.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Written informed consent.
All patients undergoing cardiac surgery with the use of cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB).
Exclusion criteria:
1. Expected non-compliance with the study protocol.
2. Any form of renal replacement therapy (e.g., maintenance hemodialysis for chronic kidney disease stage G5d, peritoneal dialysis) or previous kidney transplantation.
3. Patients with acute kidney injury (AKI) diagnosed within 30 days prior to surgery according to the KDIGO criteria.
